source_text: In Islamic traditions during the medieval period, hadith collections such as those in Sunan al-Fitra emphasized male circumcision (khitan) as one of the natural inclinations (fitrah) promoting bodily cleanliness and purity, aligning with broader ideals of hygiene that extended to aesthetic perceptions of a refined, groomed appearance. [9]
